paper_metadata.title: Effect of the c¢ Precipitate Redissolution Rate on the Microstructure and Creep Deformation Mechanism of a Second-Generation Single-Crystal Superalloy
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance

evidence.quote: A novel determination for optimal heat treatment for Ni-based single-crystal superalloys was proposed in the present work to optimize the strengthening effects of refractory elements.
The experimental alloy in question is a domestically developed low-density, second-generation nickel-based SX superalloy, and its nominal chemical composition is shown in Table 1.

The master alloy was first melted in a vacuum induction furnace (ZG-0.01) and then remelted in a directional solidification furnace (HRS) to prepare [001]-oriented single-crystal rods by the crystal selection method.

The master alloy was first melted in a vacuum induction furnace (ZG-0.01) and then remelted in a directional solidification furnace (HRS) to prepare [001]-oriented single-crystal rods by the crystal selection method.
The solid solution heat treatment of this experimental superalloy was decided based on previous work, as follows: 1310 °C/2 h + 1320 °C/4 h, followed by air cooling (AC)
The microstructure after different aging heat treatments consisted of the typical two-phase structure, with the cubic c¢ phase coherently precipitated from the c matrix.
at 1080 °C, the average size of the c¢ phase is the smallest (0.39 lm) and the cubicity is the worst.
As the temperature was increased to 1100 °C and 1120 °C, the uniformity of the c¢ phase distribution and cubicity were improved, with the increased average size of 0.43 lm and 0.45 lm, respectively.
Noteworthy, the c¢ particles at 1120 °C were spheroidized, which significantly decreased the cubicity and induced the formation of a ﬁne secondary c¢ phase in the c matrix channels.
At 1140 °C and 1160 °C, the cubicity of the c¢ phase was improved again, exhibiting the continuous increment of average size to 0.47 lm and 0.50 lm, respectively.
